t: An Mbundu kingdom in the highlands of northern Angola whose rulers’ title, ngola, gave the country of Angola its name.
From 1579 it fought Portuguese Angola, winning at Lukala in 1590 but seeing its capital, Kabasa, sacked after 1617.
Queen Njinga resisted from 1624 to 1656, allied with Matamba, the Imbangala and the Dutch; Pungo Andongo fell in 1671.
dyk: The ‘20. and odd’ Africans landed in English Virginia in August 1619 were probably captives from Portuguese campaigns against Ndongo, shipped from Luanda on a slave ship bound for Veracruz.
ev: The ngola sends envoys to Portugal asking for missionaries
A Portuguese embassy under Paulo Dias de Novais arrives in Ndongo
Ngola Kilombo kia Kasenda has the Portuguese at Kabasa killed, starting a long war
Ndongo and Matamba rout a Portuguese army at the Battle of Lukala
Njinga Mbande negotiates peace in Luanda and is baptised as Ana de Sousa
Portugal makes war on Njinga and sets up rival kings at Pungo Andongo
Njinga and her Dutch allies defeat the Portuguese at the Battle of Kombi
The Portuguese take Pungo Andongo, ending the Kingdom of Ndongo

f.capital: Kabasa; from 1626 Pungo Andongo (Ngola Hari’s line), while Njinga ruled from the Kindonga islands and later Matamba
f.founder: Ngola Kiluanje (Ngola Inene), according to tradition
f.predecessor: Mbundu chiefdoms under the overlordship of the Kingdom of Kongo
f.successor: Portuguese Angola; the Kingdom of Matamba (Njinga’s line)
